facts.fact: The official walking itinerary links River Street with squares and Forsyth Park.
facts.excerpt: Cross West Gaston Street and the northern entrance to Forsyth Park opens before you.

facts.fact: Chippewa Square was designed in1815 and named for the1812war battle.
facts.excerpt: Designed in 1815, Chippewa Square was named to commemorate the Battle of Chippewa during the War of 1812.

facts.fact: Oglethorpe is the central bronze statue in Chippewa Square.
facts.excerpt: At its center stands a bronze statue of General James Edward Oglethorpe

facts.fact: The Forrest Gump bench is no longer on the square; the bus-stop scenes used its north side.
facts.excerpt: While the famous bench now resides in a museum

facts.fact: River Street connections include old ramps and stone stairways, with the Bull Street Ramp an alternative route to examine.
facts.excerpt: follow the curve toward Bull Street Ramp for a slower climb to Bay Street.

facts.fact: Factors Walk is associated with nineteenth-century cotton pricing.
facts.excerpt: Factors Walk to the left — where cotton was once priced during the 19th century.
